title: Chander Pahar

author.name: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
author.bio: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay (1894–1950) was a celebrated Bengali author, best known for his vivid nature-inspired epics and adventurous realism including Pather Panchali and Chander Pahar.

description: Young Bengali adventurer Shankar Roy Choudhury leaves the quiet countryside of Bengal to pursue an adventurous career in the wilderness of British East Africa. Guided by Portuguese explorer Diego Alvarez, Shankar embarks on an arduous expedition across the desolate Richtersveld mountains and the scorching Kalahari in search of the legendary diamond mines of the Mountain of the Moon, guarded by the mythical beast Bunyip.
short_description: Shankar's perilous quest across the African wilderness in search of the mythical diamond-laden Mountain of the Moon.
semanticDocument:

Author: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
Category: Adventure & Thriller, Classic Bengali Literature
Language: Bengali (বাংলা)
Setting & Atmosphere: African wilderness, Uganda railway, Richtersveld mountains, Kalahari desert, dangerous diamond caves
Themes & Mood: Courage, discovery, survival expedition, mythical monster Bunyip, adrenaline, perseverance, exploration
Synopsis: Shankar leaves Bengal for Africa, teaming up with explorer Alvarez to locate the hidden diamond mines of the Mountain of the Moon while evading deadly black mambas and the ferocious Bunyip.
Tags: adventure, thriller, africa, jungle, survival, classic bengali, shankar, bunyip, diamonds

title: Srikanto

author.name: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
author.bio: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay (1876–1938) was one of Bengal's most popular novelists, known for his deep emotional insight, romantic realism, and empathetic portrayal of rural society and outcasts.

description: The episodic, reflective memoir of Srikanto, a wandering bohemian traveler navigating the hypocrisies of traditional society, turbulent romantic longings, and friendships with unconventional souls like Indranath and Annadadidi in early 20th-century Bengal.
short_description: The wandering reflections and unforgettable encounters of Srikanto, Bengali literature's quintessential bohemian traveler.
semanticDocument:
Title: Srikanto (শ্রীকান্ত)
Author: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay
Category: Classic Literature, Romance & Drama
Language: Bengali (বাংলা)
Setting & Atmosphere: Rural Bengal, Ganges river banks, bohemian voyages, nocturnal fishing expeditions
Themes & Mood: Wanderlust, human compassion, rebellion against social orthodoxy, deep unspoken love, nostalgia
Synopsis: Srikanto chronicles his youth and wanderings, from nocturnal escapades with the fearless Indranath to complex emotional bonds with outcasts and society rebels.
Tags: classic, bengali, sarat chandra, indranath, memoir, river, journey, emotion

title: Kabuliwala & Selected Stories

author.name: Rabindranath Tagore
author.bio: Rabindranath Tagore (1861–1941) was a Nobel laureate polymath whose profound poetry, short stories, and music reshaped Bengali literature and culture.

description: A collection of Rabindranath Tagore's timeless short stories led by Kabuliwala, the poignant tale of Rahamat, a dried-fruit seller from Afghanistan in 19th-century Calcutta, whose paternal bond with little Mini transcends geographic, cultural, and temporal boundaries.
short_description: Tagore's timeless masterpieces exploring paternal love, social longing, and the human heart.

title: Abol Tabol

author.name: Sukumar Ray
author.bio: Sukumar Ray (1887–1923) was Bengal's greatest master of nonsense verse, humorous satire, and children's literature, whose sharp wit and linguistic virtuosity remain peerless.

description: Sukumar Ray's crowning collection of 46 nonsense rhyming poems and illustrations, blending whimsical imagination, musical rhythm, and sharp political and social satire under the guise of delightful children's verse.
short_description: The supreme masterpiece of Bengali nonsense verse, musical rhythm, and whimsical satire.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles

author.bio: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle (1859–1930) was a Scottish writer best known for creating the legendary consulting detective Sherlock Holmes and his steadfast chronicler Dr. John Watson.

description: Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson investigate the chilling legend of a diabolical hound terrorizing the wealthy Baskerville family across the grim, fog-drenched moors of Devonshire following the mysterious death of Sir Charles Baskerville.
short_description: Sherlock Holmes confronts an ancient supernatural curse and a spectral hound on the desolate Devon moors.

short_description: In 1922 Long Island, mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby throws extravagant parties in pursuit of lost love.

title: Pather Panchali

author.name: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay
author.bio: Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay (1894–1950) was a celebrated Bengali author, best known for his vivid nature-inspired epics and adventurous realism including Pather Panchali and Chander Pahar.

description: The lyrical, heartbreaking depiction of childhood wonder and quiet rural hardship in early 20th-century Bengal through the eyes of young Apu and his free-spirited elder sister Durga in their ancestral village of Nischindipur.
short_description: The immortal Bengali masterpiece chronicling the childhood joys and struggles of Apu and Durga in rural Bengal.
